endorsements.quote: We recommend that, where possible, AI models are trained and evaluated using data that includes subcategories based on these features, ensuring increased equitability in the data and coverage of image heterogeneities; or, where not possible, that the subcategories for which the AI model is valid are clearly defined.
It is vital that a dataset is characterised, either to indicate the relevance of the training set and/or the image set that the AI will be applied to.
Therefore, appropriate coverage in the training and evaluation data is essential to obtain robust, generalisable, and equitable AI models.
We argue that it is important to test any model fully on available categories alongside a sensitivity analysis before deployment.

unlisted_practices: Define subgroups by ethnicity and age when evaluating AI software for reasons of equity.

Subgroup evaluation data by compressed breast thickness, image processing settings, compression paddle type, breast positioning, mammographic views, and presence of implants or medical devices when training and evaluating AI software.
Either remove images with implants or medical devices from AI training sets or create an appropriate training subset for them.
Avoid using scanned film images for AI model training.
Employ strict inclusion/exclusion criteria, training schemes and tailored evaluation metrics when subgroups have small sample sizes.
Enable identification and exclusion of images not of diagnostic quality and out-of-distribution views when applying AI tools.

screen.reason: The paper provides guidance and recommendations on subcategorising metadata (demographic and technical features) in training and validation datasets for healthcare AI, using mammography as a case study.
